newsitem.title: USA: Jury to resume deliberations in "Jenny Jones" trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury to resume deliberations in "Jenny Jones" trial.

text.p: Jurors in the trial of "Jenny Jones" talkshow guest Jonathan Schmitz were to resume deliberations Tuesday after reporting last week they were deadlocked.

On Friday, after six and a half hours of deliberation, the jurors sent Oakland County Circuit Judge Francis O'Brien a note saying they were unable to reach a unanimous decision and had come to a standstill. But the judge ordered the jury to take three days off and return to deliberating on Tuesday.

Schmitz, 26, was charged with first-degree murder in the shotgun slaying of Scott Amedure, 32. Schmitz confessed to shooting Amedure twice on March 9, 1995, three days after Amedure revealed he had a crush on Schmitz during a segment of the "Jenny Jones" show on same-sex secret admirers.
Schmitz' defence maintained that the humiliation he suffered from the show, coupled with mental illnesses at the time of the shooting, robbed him of the ability to form an intent to murder.

If jurors accept his defence, they can find him not guilty or guilty of second-degree murder, voluntary manslaughter, a misdemeanor charge of reckless use of a firearm causing death, or discharge of a firearm causing injury while intentionally aimed without malice, also a misdemeanor.
